claims.text: The as-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has fine, homogeneous grains.
The unchanged alloy has a high caloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor fracture toughness, crack resistance, and load-bearing integrity.
Annealing below the full-recrystallization point followed by quenching or controlled cooling can produce a heterogeneous grain structure in this alloy.
The resulting heterogeneous structure will contain both coarse- and fine-grained regions.
The heterogeneous grain-size distribution will impede crack initiation and propagation.
Grain-boundary strengthening and energy dissipation are the mechanisms by which the heterogeneous grain structure will improve crack resistance.
Partial recrystallization annealing will preserve the phase microstructures responsible for the caloric effect.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the annealed alloy will have greater fracture toughness and load-bearing capacity.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the annealed alloy will retain its caloric response with no more than a minimal reduction under the same magnetic-field and pressure-field conditions.
The intervention is intended to apply under the magnetic fields, pressure fields, temperatures, and mechanical loads typical of solid-state refrigeration operation.
Excessive grain coarsening may compromise the caloric response.
An integrity improvement of no more than 5%, or a caloric-performance reduction greater than 5%, is stipulated as a result that would falsify the hypothesis.
